findings.title: Completed reschedules bypass the deferred SendGrid cancellation path
findings.body: Passing `true` invokes the immediate branch of `deleteScheduledEmailReminder`, which posts `status: "cancel"` to SendGrid immediately and returns without marking or deleting the WorkflowReminder. This runs for every completed reschedule regardless of how far in the future the reminder is, so cancelled batches remain pending in SendGrid until their send time and consume the 100 pending-cancellation limit this change is intended to avoid. Reschedules that do not first pass through `requestReschedule` also leave the reminder row uncancelled and stale. Use the deferred `cancelled` state here (or only use an immediate cancellation for a near-term deadline) so the cron owns the final SendGrid request and cleanup.

findings.title: Polling cancellation leaves reminders scheduled during the cron interval
findings.body: A cancellation only sets `cancelled` in the database; this code does not call SendGrid until the next cron invocation. If a booking is cancelled after one 15-minute run and its reminder is due before the next run, SendGrid will send the email before this query sees it. On the next run the earlier cleanup deletes records whose scheduled date is already past, so the external scheduled send is never cancelled at all. Querying one hour ahead does not close this gap because the row was not marked cancelled at the prior run. The cancellation flow needs a safe immediate path for reminders due before the next run, or a cancellation job/timing guarantee that runs before every possible send time.

findings.title: Reminder cancellation persistence is launched but never awaited
findings.body: `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are async and perform the database update/delete needed to stop or queue the reminder, but the nested `forEach` discards their promises. The later `Promise.all` does not include these operations, so this handler can return while the email's `cancelled` flag has not been written (or a serverless runtime can terminate the work). A cron run or an imminent SendGrid send can therefore observe the reminder as active and send it. Collect these promises and await them before completing the cancellation request.

findings.title: One failed SendGrid cancellation prevents all later reminders from being cancelled
findings.body: The single `try` covers the whole sequential loop. If `client.request` rejects for one reminder (for example, a missing or already-expired SendGrid batch), control jumps to the outer catch and every remaining `remindersToCancel` entry is skipped. Those later reminders remain scheduled and can still be sent; the bad row can also block the same batch again on subsequent cron runs. Handle errors per reminder and continue processing the remaining rows, deleting only rows whose cancellation succeeded.
